newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia aims to cool China rift over Dalai Lama.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia aims to cool China rift over Dalai Lama.

text.p: Australia tried on Thursday to cool a row with China over a planned meeting later in the day between Prime Minister John Howard and Tibet's exiled spiritual leader the Dalai Lama.
Hours before the meeting in Howard's Sydney office (0700 GMT), Foreign Minister Alexander Downer called for mutual understanding between Beijing and Canberra.

"We have our values in Australia and obviously we will uphold our values, and that's a point I've made clear to the Chinese government in Beijing," Downer told Australia Broadcasting Corporation radio from New York.
"We understand their position. We hope they will understand ours."
China on Tuesday threatened unspecified trade sanctions against Australia after Howard's office said he would meet the Tibetan Buddhist god-king despite Chinese protests.

Beijing considers the Dalai Lama, who fled Tibet in 1959 after an abortive uprising against Chinese rule and won the Nobel Peace Prize 30 years later for his peaceful autonomy campaign, to be a separatist troublemaker.
Downer said Australia had recognised Tibet as a part of China since 1972 and did not support calls for it to become an independent state.
"We don't support a separate Tibetan state, we never have done since Australia recognised China, and we see the Dalai Lama as a religious leader," he said.
"So we say to the Chinese government that our relationship must be based on mutual understanding of our political systems and mutual understanding of our respective values."

Asked about the Chinese threats, he added: "I am sorry there have been threats of possible sanctions but as a country we do have values and it's important that the Australian government upholds Australian values."
Downer said it remained to be seen whether Beijing would carry through on its threatened trade retaliation.
Earlier on Thursday, Howard won support for his position from Hollywood heartthrob Richard Gere, a Buddhist who campaigns for Tibetan human rights.
"The Prime Minister John Howard has shown an incredible courage in welcoming His Holiness," Gere told ABC radio.
"There are nations in this world who will not do the right thing for fear of retribution from the Chinese."
But Gere said Howard would have shown even greater courage if he had agreed to meet the Dalai Lama as the leader of Tibet itself rather than as a spiritual leader.
